The tricky part: optimal grouping. The classic solution is a greedy algorithm that takes one of each book at a time and sorts by count. Key insight: when there are 3 books with the maximum count, the optimal strategy is to take one of each of the top 4 books (so that a group of 4 can be formed, since 4+4 is cheaper than 5+3).

Standard greedy algorithm:
- Count each book.
- While any count is greater than 0:
  - Sort counts in descending order.
  - Determine group size: normally take one from each book that has count > 0. However, if the number of books with count equal to the max count is 3, take 4 instead of 3 (i.e., also include the next book down).
